evals.name: bioma-project-page
evals.prompt: Write the project page for Bioma Costa del Este
evals.expected_output: A project page for /projects/bioma-costa-del-este following the site's structured field schema: title, meta_description, hook, body, suits, drawbacks, location_note, buying_note, faqs, sources. Includes a per-unit price/floor-plan table, a specific hook paragraph, at least one sourced drawback, 3+ FAQs from real buyer questions, and every figure sourced to a primary institution with a check date.
expectations: Output is delivered as separate structured fields (title, meta_description, hook, body, suits, drawbacks, location_note, buying_note, faqs, sources) rather than one undifferentiated blob of markdown
Includes a per-unit price and floor-plan table (beds, baths, m²/sq ft, price)
The hook paragraph names one specific, verifiable fact about Bioma Costa del Este (a permit, license, developer track record, or price anomaly) rather than generic marketing language
At least one drawback is named and is attributed to a source other than the developer (UGC, forum, or reasoned risk) rather than a generic hedge like 'may not suit everyone'
At least 3 FAQs are present, phrased as real buyer questions
At least one figure (price, tax, or fee) carries a named source and a check date/month, not just a bare number
No unsourced currency-conversion phrasing (e.g. '$X USD (approximately...)')
Body prose (excluding the price table) is substantive, not a thin 150-word placeholder

evals.name: boquete-area-page
evals.prompt: We need the Boquete area page written
evals.expected_output: An area page for /areas/boquete following the site's area-page structure: identity, positioning, a sourced 'Is Boquete titled?' section, cost-of-living figures with sources, who it suits and who it doesn't, getting there/around, and an FAQ. Avoids travel-writing filler and answers purchase questions.
expectations: Includes a dedicated, sourced section addressing title status / titled land vs Rights of Possession risk specific to Boquete
Includes at least one concrete cost-of-living or cost-to-buy figure with a named source
Includes an explicit 'who this suits / who it doesn't' section naming a type of buyer it is NOT good for
Includes practical access information (distance/time to nearest airport, road quality, whether a car is required)
At least 3 FAQs are present
The page does not spend more than a sentence or two on scenery/atmosphere description disconnected from a purchase question (avoids travel-writing drift)

evals.name: titled-vs-rop-guide
evals.prompt: Draft the guide on titled land vs Rights of Possession in Panama
evals.expected_output: A buying guide following the guide structure: opening paragraph leading with a number/fact, a Key Takeaways box (4-6 sourced bullets), a body with H2s per stage/question and tables where useful, callouts, a 'when the honest answer is don't' section, numbered sources with full URLs to primary institutions (ANATI, Registro Público, Gaceta Oficial), and an FAQ.
expectations: Opens with a specific fact or number in the first sentence rather than throat-clearing scene-setting
Includes a Key Takeaways section with 4-6 bullets, each carrying a source
Explains the practical difference between titled land and Rights of Possession (ANATI-administered) with correct, non-generic detail
Includes a section equivalent to 'when the honest answer is don't' — a case where the guide recommends against a Rights of Possession purchase or flags real risk
Sources are numbered/listed with named primary institutions (ANATI and/or Registro Público and/or Gaceta Oficial), not just 'various sources' or broker sites
Spanish/legal terms (finca, ANATI, Registro Público, derechos posesorios) are defined on first use
At least 3 FAQs are present
